problem: The tree puts 'Procedural' only under 3D, but the chapter itself treats procedural rules (for example the bobbing float h = A sin 2πft) as a way to drive any motion, 2D or 3D. The tree also mixes two different classifications in one split: 2D/3D are rendering techniques, while keyframe, procedural and mocap are motion drivers that cut across both.
fix: Label the leaves so the mixing is clear, e.g. '3D rig (keys / procedural / mocap)' and note in the caption that procedural rules and mocap data drive 2D motion as well, while the 2D/3D split is about how frames are produced.

problem: 'Rendering is always last' contradicts the chapter's own tool list, where compositors combine renders with live plates after rendering. A student can read this as saying nothing happens after the render.
fix: Write 'rendering is the last of the six stages and is done per frame; compositing can follow it'.

problem: The bullet is named Lighting but also assigns camera placement, which is a separate job. Students revising stage order will think cameras are part of lighting.
fix: Split it: 'Lighting: place and tune lights for the shot. Camera: set the camera position, lens and framing (Unit 3).' If a six-stage list must be kept, say 'Lighting and camera: place lights and set the camera for the shot (Unit 3)'.

problem: 12.5 frames/s is an instant between two frames, so 'frame 12 or 13' is ambiguous and depends on whether frames are numbered from 0 or from 1. A student cannot tell which frame holds t = 0.5 s.
fix: State the numbering and give the bracket, e.g. 'At 25 fps, t = 0.5 s falls halfway between two frames: with frames numbered 0, 1, 2 …, it lies between frame 12 (t = 0.48 s) and frame 13 (t = 0.52 s).'
